The court's running caption spells it 'Ojay' (stamped pp.108, 111, 119) but the clerk's endorsements use 'Ojai'; register 'Ojai' matches.

year.evidence: no concession decree or expediente translation appears in images 112-130 (stamped pp.103-121); that whole stretch is 1856-1866 District Court paper. The grant decree sits in the unread front of the file and digicoll could not be re-fetched, so 1837 was not tested.

governor.evidence: same stretch as year: no concession decree in stamped pp.103-121, and Alvarado is nowhere named in the pages read.

grantee.evidence: stamped 168 SD p.108 (image 117), motion of Juan Camarillo: 'successor in interest in the tract called and known as "Ojay" in Santa Barbara County, to Fernando Tico, the original grantee named in the record in this cause'; repeated in the decree at stamped p.119 (image 128): 'Fernando Tico the original grantee of the tract called "Ojay"'. This is a judicial recital in a signed decree, not the concession decree itself, which was not reachable - but it decisively excludes the dominant error class, because the court expressly separates Tico (original grantee) from Camarillo (U.S.-era claimant substituted of record).

land_case.evidence: page stamps read '168 SD' throughout (e.g. stamped p.103 = image 112); caption at stamped p.108 (image 117): 'Docket No. 168 / Land Com. No. 139'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd168.pdf.

outcome.evidence: District Court decree of 16 June 1862, stamped 168 SD p.113 (image 122), orders a new survey 'in conformity to the decree of this Court confirming the title of said claim to the claimant' - a District Court confirmation is recited as already entered. Clerk's endorsement, stamped p.114 (image 123): 'Fernando Tico vs United States / Decree / Filed June 16, 1862'. Confirmation established; the confirmation decree itself and the 1870 patent lie outside the pages read.

notes: Gradeable only because a prior agent (work-B211) had already cut images 112-130 out of cubanc_lcf_sd168.pdf and left the excerpt on disk; nothing new could be fetched from digicoll (see chunk-level note in record rancho-pauma). Stamped-vs-image drift in this file is a constant 9 (image 112 = stamped PAGE 103); no duplicate exposure in this stretch. ** FLAG FOR PHASE C: the register's patent_to 'Fernando Tico' looks wrong on the face of this file. ** Tico conveyed Ojai to Henry S. Carnes 25 May 1853 (recited stamped p.104, image 113); Carnes and his wife Domitila Rodriguez de Carnes conveyed to Juan Camarillo 24 June 1856 (deed at stamped pp.104-106, images 113-115); the District Court in June 1862 substituted 'the name of Juan Camarillo ... as the real party in interest ... for, and in lieu of that of Fernando Tico' (stamped pp.119-120, images 128-129); and on 26 Sept 1866 John Wyeth and John B. Church swore they 'have become owners of premises of the above entitled Rancho' (stamped p.115, image 124). A patent issuing 22 Dec 1870 to Fernando Tico personally is therefore doubtful and should be checked against the GLO record rather than assumed. Two further facts of record: the posture 'Fernando Tico, appellee, ads The United States, appellant' in the Oct. 1864 term (stamped p.117, image 126) is the ordinary U.S. appeal from the Commission, not a reversal; and the 16 June 1862 decree annulled the Mandeville survey as 'not in accordance with the grant, nor in conformity to the decree of this Court confirming the same', which is why the patent came so late.
